86a1903adb53184fa1a8470d5f6fba7fa7b13d6e.summary: Trend Micro's TrendLabs blog post, published 2012-12-21, describes the Dexter malware (BKDR_DEXTR.A). It is a data stealer that targets point-of-sale systems used at hotels and other businesses, and it sends collected information to a remote server. The executable is packed or encrypted to hinder analysis. The report says the initial infection vector was still undetermined.

The report says the stolen data is presumably duplicated by remote malicious users.
The report says the obfuscation was probably done to make analysis difficult.
The report presents the list of stealable data as possible data, not confirmed data.

86e496f986f55f6c0b0191ce30111a6769ca7696.summary: S2W analysis of a 2020 watering-hole attack on a North Korea-related website, visited by users of an older Internet Explorer. Multi-stage Ruby and PE loaders decrypt a final payload, a variant of ROKRAT that steals files, browser and mail data, takes screenshots and logs keys. It uses legitimate cloud services (pCloud, Yandex, Box, Dropbox, Backblaze B2) for command and control. The report judges the activity to be related to Scarcruft (APT37, Group123), which it describes as linked to North Korea and active since 2012.

86dcb88e8ad174d9169c965836b00c32697ebb17.summary: AhnLab ASEC describes a campaign called KONO DIO DA that targets poorly managed Linux SSH servers through dictionary attacks. It installs XMRig CoinMiner under a disguised process name, drops SHC-built downloader scripts, and creates a backdoor SSH account. Past cases also used a planted SSH key, cron persistence and disabled security tools. The report recommends strong, changed passwords, patching, firewalls and updating the V3 product.
